title: Minimum Sum of Four Digit Number After Splitting Digits
summary: Given a positive integer num consisting of exactly four digits, split num into two new integers new1 and new2 by using the digits found in num.
statement: Given a positive integer num consisting of exactly four digits, split num into two new integers new1 and new2 by using the digits found in num. Leading zeros are allowed in new1 and new2, and all the digits from num must be used. For example, given num = 2932, the digits are two 2's, one 9, and one 3. Possible pairs of new1 and new2 include [22, 93], [23, 92], [223, 9], and [2, 329]. The task is to find the pair that results in the minimum possible sum of new1 and new2.
constraints: num has exactly four decimal digits; repeated digits and zero digits are allowed.
Use all four digits in two new integers; leading zeros are allowed.
hints: Tens-place digits contribute ten times as much as ones-place digits.
Sort the four digits and assign the two smallest to the two tens places.
Any larger tens digit can be exchanged with a smaller ones digit to reduce the sum, proving the greedy placement.
editorial: Any larger tens digit can be exchanged with a smaller ones digit to reduce the sum, proving the greedy placement.

tests.explanation: Sorting gives 2,2,3,9; putting 2 and 2 in the tens places produces 23+29=52.
The two smallest digits are zeros, so 04+09 gives 13.
